net_debt_bridge.note: Lease treatment (B): lease principal is charged in the flows (lease_cost_pct 0.4% of revenue), so the $1.14m of lease liabilities is EXCLUDED from net debt. Contingent consideration ($3.85m, Oral Science royalty to 2033, max $6.0m) is debt-like and included. Net cash $6.39m.

inputs.finance_income_note: FY2025 finance income was $0.886m, but RX.V's reported OCF already EXCLUDES net finance income of $0.760m (IFRS presentation) -- the operating flow is clean, so nothing is stripped here (stripping again would double-deduct). The matching assets (cash + ST + LT investments, $12.24m at Jun-2026) sit in the net-debt bridge per the excluded-income/matching-asset rule (owner-fcf.md 7d).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual filing cash flow statement, share-based payment expense $624,613; no separate equity-award tax withholding disclosed
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 NCIB $0.215m; H1-2026 stepped up 14x to $3.09m alongside repaying $6m of the $8m acquisition facilities. NCIB shrank the count from ~14.5m (FY2018) to 11.26m (FY2025); 234,192 consideration shares issued Mar-2026 mean the count is no longer falling.
inputs.share_count_basis: Q2-2026 basic weighted average 11,393,271 (per user instruction), which already includes the 234,192 Oral Science consideration shares. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count) and the active NCIB funds the flat count. Diluted count ~11.5m (options); using basic is ~1% generous per share.
inputs.last_fcf_note: Owner FCF FY2025 = OCF 9.009 - capex 0.390 (PP&E 0.054 + intangibles 0.336) - SBC 0.625 - lease principal 0.197 = 7.798 ($0.69/sh). This is a PEAK (1.8x the FY2019-25 owner-FCF median of ~4.3) and is NOT projected forward -- the component build derives Y1 FCF from revenue x normalized components instead (Y1 owner-FCF margin 12.7% vs FY2025's 18.1%).
inputs.dividend_note: Quarterly $0.055 (+10% in 2026), ~1.4% yield; paid out of the modelled FCF, not additive to it.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-08-26T19:59:30Z regular close 15.84; working price 15.70 per orchestrator instruction
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF (operating company; specialty pharma in-licensor/distributor), routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md; non-US filer so section 7 of owner-fcf.md applied. Component build, 10-year horizon. CRITICAL: the FY2025 balance sheet is stale -- the 2026-03-01 Oral Science acquisition ($31.48m total consideration incl. $3.85m contingent) collapsed net cash from $31.1m to ~$6.4m (treatment-B basis); the bridge uses the 2026-06-30 balance sheet. Margins are built from the NEW post-acquisition blend (H1-2026 GM 71.5%, OM 21.0%, EBITDA ~25.5%), not FY2025's 76.6%/26.0%. Lease treatment (B): principal in flows, liabilities out of net debt. Risk placement: customer concentration and illiquidity live in the WACC; licence-termination/launch-failure/PPA-impairment risk lives in the bear-case flows and its elevated 25% weight -- each charged exactly once (7f).

wacc_rationale.currency: CAD flows discounted at a CAD-built rate (GoC 10y ~3.4% risk-free + ~5.5% ERP + small-cap size premium = ~10.5% Canadian small-cap base)
wacc_rationale.notes: Concentration premium (+2.0): four pharmacy-wholesaler customers = 77.1% of FY2025 revenue, largest 34.2% -- past the >40% single-customer threshold in the Step 8c.5 template. Illiquidity (+1.0): ~CAD $177m market cap, TSXV, sparse coverage. Licence dependence and provisional-PPA impairment risk are deliberately NOT in the WACC -- they are charged in the bear scenario's flows and its elevated 25% weight (risk charged once, owner-fcf.md 7f). Same WACC for all three scenarios.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 9.1% vs revenue 14.0% (>30% divergence): equity growth is depressed by ~$4.5m/yr of dividends + NCIB buybacks, so it understates business growth; EPS CAGR 22.5% is flattered by the 19% share-count shrink since 2019. Organic forward growth is set between them (8% -> 3%).
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs computed on the owner-FCF series (OCF - PP&E&intangible capex - SBC - lease principal): FY2020 6.43 -> FY2025 7.80 = 3.9%/yr, far below the reported-FCF 5.4%/yr and wildly below the 3yr 22.2% (FY2022 trough to FY2025 peak). The owner series is noisy because product-rights purchases are lumpy (FY2024 $4.63m, FY2025 $0.34m) -- exactly why reinvestment is normalized at 2% of revenue in the projection.

base.narrative: Oral Science annualizes in FY2026 (~+67% reported revenue) at the new blended margin structure (~25% EBITDA, ~71% gross), then growth reverts to the organic mid-single-digit path: FeraMAX Pd defends its #1 recommended-brand status against private-label entry, Tibella and international grow off small bases, Thyconvi launches to a modest but real contribution, and Oral Health grows at Canadian dental-category rates. Margins hold at the post-acquisition blend with slight scale gains; reinvestment is normalized at 2% of revenue to reflect the periodic product-rights purchases (FY2024: $4.6m) that FY2025's $0.39m understates.

bull.narrative: Thyconvi -- the only liquid levothyroxine in Canada, with no direct competitor -- becomes a durable multi-million franchise; Oral Science integration yields cross-selling into BioSyent's pharmacy relationships and EBITDA margin recovers toward 28% as the Oral Health book scales; international (Tibelia global rights) keeps compounding off its small base. Growth holds high-single/low-double-digit for five years before maturing.

bear.narrative: The pattern of Gelclair (discontinued Aug-2026) and Combogesic (rights returned Sept-2025) repeats: Thyconvi launch spend is expensed but the product does not convert; a licensor terminates or repatriates one meaningful in-licensed product; private-label pressure clips FeraMAX growth to zero; Oral Science proves ex-growth and part of the provisional $22.9m of acquired intangibles+goodwill is impaired (a non-cash marker of the same lost flows this path already prices). Revenue stalls after the acquisition annualizes and EBITDA margin compresses to 22%.

entry_price.note: Entry = (PV of interim owner FCF at 15% + WACC-based terminal value discounted at 15% - net debt) / shares, per scenario, probability-weighted 25/50/25.

required_return_table.note: 13.5% is the model's own WACC. At the current $15.70 the base-case path implies a forward return of roughly 8.5-9%.

sensitivity.note: Base scenario. Rows = WACC, columns = terminal growth. Even at WACC 11.5% / g 3.5% the base case reaches only $14.83, below the $15.70 price.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: BioSyent owns little core IP (in-licensed portfolio is terminable), the organic launch record is genuinely mixed (Gelclair discontinued Aug-2026, Combogesic rights returned Sept-2025, FY2024 $0.43m impairment), and 72.7% of the provisional Oral Science PPA is intangibles+goodwill the filing itself warns may change materially. Bull cut to 25% because it needs Thyconvi success AND Oral Science integration AND continued FeraMAX defence simultaneously. These risks are priced here in the flows/weights, not in the WACC (charged once).
probability_weighted.band_note: SBC is only ~1% of revenue so the house/street band is just $0.68 wide ($11.18-$11.86); the $15.70 price sits ~6.7 band-widths ABOVE the street ceiling -- the gap to price is a valuation gap, not an SBC-accounting gap.

sanity_check.diagnosis: Preemptive fixes applied at build time rather than after a trip: (1) peak-earnings extrapolation -- FY2025 owner FCF $7.80m is 1.8x the FY2019-25 median ~$4.3m, so the model does NOT project from it; the component build yields a Y1 owner-FCF margin of 12.7% vs FY2025's 18.1%, with reinvestment normalized at 2% of revenue vs FY2025's 0.9% (FY2024 spent $4.67m); (2) structural WACC understatement -- +2.0% customer concentration (four customers 77.1%, largest 34.2%) and +1.0% TSXV micro-cap illiquidity on a 10.5% CAD small-cap base = 13.5%.
sanity_check.fix_applied: Mid-cycled via component margins + normalized reinvestment; WACC premiums +3.0% total; bear weight 25%. With base upside at -27.4% the price-percentile trip (upside >100% at the 99th percentile of the 10y range) cannot fire.
sanity_check.verdict: PASS. Implied base-case multiples (P/E ~15.3x FY2025-adj / ~13.2x TTM, P/B 2.83x, EV/EBITDA 10.8x) all sit BELOW the 10-year averages (P/E 19.7x, P/B 3.45x) and far below the bounds (P/E<39.4x, P/B<6.41x). The market at $15.70 is paying 19.6x earnings and 4.26x book -- its 10-year P/B maximum -- for the post-acquisition entity at structurally LOWER margins than the history that earned those multiples.

valuation_philosophy: This model deliberately values BioSyent as an income-plus-modest-growth compounder, not a multi-bagger: mid-cycle owner economics (normalized 2%-of-revenue reinvestment instead of FY2025's unusually light $0.39m; post-acquisition blended margins of ~25% EBITDA instead of the pre-deal 28%), a 13.5% CAD WACC carrying explicit concentration and illiquidity premiums, and a 25% bear weight carrying the licence-termination/launch-failure/PPA-impairment risk. On that basis the stock is worth ~$11.2 weighted (~$11.4 base) against a $15.70 price sitting at the 99th percentile of its 10-year range and at its 10-year maximum P/B. The market is extrapolating the +59.7% H1-2026 headline revenue growth; earnings grew only +19.7% because the acquisition bought revenue at materially lower margin. Buying here requires believing the bull case (Thyconvi franchise + Oral Science synergies + margin recovery to 28%), which is worth $14.42 -- still below the price.
